rainfall.en: The region received about 509.0 mm of rain per year on average over 2015-2024. Data sources agree only roughly, so treat this as a good estimate.

rainfall_trend.en: Rainfall has declined by about 44 mm per decade over 1995-2024 (two independent trend tests agree). Data sources agree well, so this number is fairly reliable.

water_stress.en: Recent years (2015-2024) were about 16% drier than the 1995-2014 average of the same region. Definition is still being confirmed by the team.

hot_days.en: During grain filling (April to June), the crop endures about 3.1 hot days (above 35.0 degrees C) per year. Data sources disagree or data is limited, so treat this as a rough indication only.

frost_days.en: Spring frost (March to April) still reaches the crop on about 4.5 nights per year. Data sources disagree or data is limited, so treat this as a rough indication only.

extreme_rain_days.en: Expect about 3.6 days per year with intense rain over 20.0 mm. Data sources disagree or data is limited, so treat this as a rough indication only.

longest_dry_spell_days.en: The longest stretch without effective rain within the growing season lasts about 23.5 days on average. Data sources disagree or data is limited, so treat this as a rough indication only.

soil.en: Soil organic matter is medium (12.52 g/kg in the top 30 cm), pH around 7.77. SoilGrids is a model estimate, not a lab measurement. Data sources agree only roughly, so treat this as a good estimate.

ndvi.en: Satellite greenness (NDVI) from the nearby 5x5 km pixel averaged over 2020-2024 suggests a yield baseline of 0.363 (0-1 scale). This is a rough proxy: no crop mask, no pixel quality filter, only 5 years. Data sources disagree or data is limited, so treat this as a rough indication only.

rainfall_source_disagreement.en: NASA POWER and ERA5 differ by under 25 percent on rainfall over 1995-2024 (574.9 vs 506.2 mm/yr). Data sources agree only roughly, so treat this as a good estimate.

sources: ICARDA WANA Long-Term Cereal-Legume Trials (30-40% synthetic N reduction post-legume; disease & wild-oat break)
ITGC Algeria Technical Itineraries (Durum Wheat, Barley, Pulses, Rapeseed/Colza, Conservation Agriculture)

nitrogen_carryover_rule.justification: ICARDA Mediterranean trials show cereals planted immediately after a food legume (faba bean, chickpea, lentil) achieve optimal yields with 30-40% less synthetic nitrogen fertilizer.

agronomic_justifications.max_occurrences_per_crop_1: Prevents pathogen spore buildup (Fusarium crown rot in wheat, Ascochyta blight in chickpea, Orobanche broomrape in faba/sunflower).
agronomic_justifications.forbid_consecutive_same_family: Puts a broadleaf legume or Brassicaceae/Asteraceae oilseed between grass cereals to suppress wild oats (Avena sterilis) and root nematodes.
agronomic_justifications.min_legumes_1: Guarantees biological nitrogen fixation (+20 to +32 kg N/ha) and breaks continuous cereal N mining.
agronomic_justifications.cyclic_3_family_note: Because a cyclic 3-year plan wraps Year 3 -> Year 1, forbidding consecutive same-family crops mathematically produces 3-family systems (1 Cereal + 1 Legume + 1 Oilseed Break Crop). On plots below 380 mm rainfall where oilseeds are not grown, farmers instead use a 2-year Cereal <-> Legume alternation.

gaps.text: Soil SOC and pH come from 250 m ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 modelled cells (0-30 cm), not a laboratory NPK soil test of your single parcel.
NASA POWER climate telemetry uses a 0.5° × 0.625° grid (~55 km), which smooths micro-valley rainfall and frost pockets.
MODIS MOD13Q1 spring peak NDVI (2020-2024, 5×5 km patch average) mixes cropland with roads and fallow; no cropland mask or pixel QA filter was applied.
Legume biological nitrogen fixation (+20 to +32 kg N/ha) is an ICARDA dryland benchmark; actual carryover depends on rhizobia nodulation and grazing management.
Gross income uses official OAIC/CCLS campaign prices (DA/q) × regional yield; net profit varies with fuel, seed, and CCLS quality grades (bonifications/réfractions).
NASA POWER shows 13-43% higher rainfall than Open-Meteo ERA5 reanalysis across the three regions; cross-check confidence labels reflect this spread.
Soil erosion risk cannot be estimated reliably from current inputs (RUSLE factors absent), so no numeric erosion claim is fabricated.
Water-stress magnitude depends on the recent comparison window (2015-2024 vs 2020-2024 sensitivity variant) while relative stress stays positive everywhere.

Water stress is computed from meteoric rainfall (NASA POWER). In irrigated regions such as the Punjab Plains (India) or irrigated pockets of the US Great Plains, canal and tube-well water mask rainfall deficits while depleting groundwater aquifers.

gaps.topic: Single Annual Crop Cycle vs Double Cropping
gaps.text: Many South Asian farms grow two crops per year (e.g. Kharif rice followed by Rabi wheat). Our engine models one primary crop per year across a 3-year sequence; multi-season double-cropping is documented as a future improvement.

Light regions (Central Kansas, USA and Punjab Plains, India) use public national datasets (USDA NASS, FAOSTAT, ICAR) without local field-trial calibration and are labeled 'Less validated'. NASA POWER grid cells (~50 km) represent flat regional farmland rather than individual parcels.

NASA FIRMS (VIIRS 375 m / MODIS 1 km) detects actively burning thermal anomalies (~3 hours latency). It is not a fire forecast or danger index; cloud cover or small fires can be missed, and industrial hotspots can appear.
